questiontext.text:
UniCV prototype for questions in which the student builds a flowchart, with blocks and rules similar to those of Flowgorithm but simpler: variables are not declared and there are no functions or arrays (for those, use unicv_flowgorithm). The grader runs the flowchart with the input of each test case and compares what it writes with the expected output, as in a programming question.

How to write a question

  1. Create a CodeRunner question of type unicv_flowchart, write the name and the question text, and save.
  2. In each test case, put the input data in Standard Input (one value per line) and the expected output in Expected output. Leave Test code empty.
  3. Build the solution flowchart in the Answer field and save with Validate on save ticked, to check that it passes the tests.
  4. For tall flowcharts, increase the number of rows of the answer box (Answer box, Rows), e.g. to 30.

What the student gets

  • An editor with the Start and End blocks. A block is inserted by clicking the "+" on an arrow, and its content is written inside the block. The available blocks are:
    • Input (Read): one or more variables, separated by commas. Each variable gets one line of the test input.
    • Output (Write): an expression, e.g. "Total: " & soma. Each block writes one line.
    • Assignment: variable = expression.
    • If: a condition, with a True branch and a False branch that join again.
    • While: repeats the blocks of the loop while the condition is true (tested before).
    • For: i = 1 até 10 (or to), optionally with passo 2 (or step; a negative step counts down).
    • Do: runs the blocks of the loop and repeats while the condition is true (tested after).
  • Above the drawing, on the right: a list to choose the language of the editor (Portuguese, English or Spanish; by default that of the Moodle page), a Start again button that removes every block except Start and End, and a Help button with the blocks, the operators and how to add and remove blocks. The colours of the blocks are those of Flowgorithm.
  • After Check, the usual CodeRunner table of tests (input, expected output and the output of the flowchart), and the reason when the flowchart cannot run (e.g. an empty block, a loop that never ends, or a block that the question requires and is missing).

Expressions

  • Numbers, texts between quotes, + - * / ^, mod (or %), div, & to join texts and values, the comparisons = == != <> < > <= >=, the logical operators e, ou, não (or and, or, not, &&, ||, !) and the values verdadeiro and falso.
  • Functions: Abs, Sqrt/Raiz, Int, Round/Arred, Max, Min, Len, ToInteger, ToReal and ToString.
  • The words e, ou, não, verdadeiro and falso are recognised only with the editor in Portuguese (in Spanish, verdadero and falso); and, or, not, true and false work in every language.
  • Real numbers with no decimal part are written without decimals (4, not 4.0).

Grading

  • Each test is passed when the output of the flowchart is exactly the expected output. With All-or-nothing grading (the default), the mark is 1 only if every test is passed.
  • The requirements in require and forbid (see below) are checked before running the tests.

Limitations

  • Variables are not declared and have no fixed type; there are no arrays and no functions defined by the student (use unicv_flowgorithm).
  • Each Output block writes a whole line; it is not possible to write several values on the same line with several blocks (join them with &).
  • The flowchart is stored as JSON in the answer; it cannot be imported from or exported to Flowgorithm (.fprg) files.

Template parameters (all optional)

  • require: list of block types that the flowchart must use, among "input", "output", "assign", "if", "while", "for", "do" and "loop" (any of the three loops).
  • forbid: list of block types that the flowchart must not use (same names). For example, {"require": ["loop"], "forbid": ["do"]} accepts a For or a While loop, but not a Do loop.
  • max_steps (default 10000): largest number of blocks run in each test, to detect endless loops.
  • lang (default "pt"): language of the question, "pt", "en" or "es". It sets how logical values are written in the output (Verdadeiro/Falso, True/False, Verdadero/Falso) and the language of the error messages when the student has not chosen another one.

Example: {"require": ["loop", "if"], "forbid": ["do"]}

Only these names, in English, are accepted. A parameter with another name, or a shape type that does not exist, is reported as a question error (and Validate on save rejects the question), so typing mistakes are not silently ignored.
